narrative.overview: Sorayori uses a Living Atmosphere design language: forecast information remains immediately legible while the surrounding weather scene communicates time, condition, and emotional tone. The system is Android-first, tactile, restrained, and cinematic without becoming decorative or data-heavy.

rules.name: Clarity Before Atmosphere
rules.body: Current conditions and the next meaningful change must remain understandable even when scene artwork and motion are removed.

rules.name: One Continuous Forecast
rules.body: The home screen reads as one unfolding weather story rather than a stack of unrelated cards.

rules.name: Weather Owns the Sky
rules.body: Scene colors may change with conditions, but content surfaces and semantic text roles remain stable.

rules.name: Restrained Accent
rules.body: Use the accent for the single most useful upcoming-weather narrative, not for decoration or repeated emphasis.

rules.name: Temperature Is the Display
rules.body: Do not introduce another display treatment that competes with the current temperature.

rules.name: Weight Builds Hierarchy
rules.body: Prefer changes in size and weight over uppercase text, decorative lettering, or excessive color.

rules.name: Progressive Disclosure
rules.body: Show humidity, wind, rain chance, and UV first. Keep secondary measurements behind the explicit details control.

rules.name: Continuous Surface
rules.body: Sunrise, daily forecast, and update status continue the details surface rather than becoming separate floating containers.

rules.name: Tactile Control
rules.body: Interactive elements must look pressable through tonal fill, shape, or position, never through decorative glow.

rules.name: Real Icon
rules.body: Use the established Lucide and Meteocons systems. Do not substitute emoji or Unicode glyphs.

rules.name: Condition Evidence
rules.body: Every major atmospheric layer must correspond to the active weather condition or time of day.

rules.name: One Authored Moment
rules.body: The hero reveal is the primary entrance. Supporting sections should not repeat the same staged animation.

rules.name: Weather Pace
rules.body: Clear and cloudy scenes move slowly, precipitation moves directionally, and storms may flash briefly without creating continuous visual noise.

rules.name: Meaning Without Motion
rules.body: No weather fact, status, or interaction may depend on animation alone.

dos: Keep current conditions and the next meaningful change immediately legible.
Use weather-specific imagery and motion as evidence of the forecast state.
Use a continuous light surface for detailed forecast information.
Honor reduced motion, safe areas, bilingual copy, and compact widths.
donts: Do not use proprietary Google or Pixel Weather assets.
Do not use aurora gradients, arbitrary abstract blobs, or unrelated stock photography.
Do not repeat the mint accent across every control.
Do not substitute emoji or Unicode glyphs for the established icon systems.
